derivation: STANDARDS-DERIVED. Every field traces to a standard, a regulation or a recognised industry body per campaign/SOURCE_AUTHORITY_PACK.md. Nothing is generalised from a client programme or a product. Field service management is not a standards domain; where the pack says so, the field is judgment and is labelled.
field_set: EN 17007:2017 cl. 5.2 maintenance process profile, corroborated by ISO 9001:2015 cl. 4.4.1 a) to h).
gaps: Field service management is not a standards domain. No ISO, IEC, CEN/EN, ANSI or IEEE standard has field service, mobile workforce management, rostering, appointment booking, travel routing or dispatch as its subject. IEC 61968-6:2015 cl. 4.2 SCHD and FRD standardise what is exchanged, not how scheduling is done. Activities in 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4 that describe matching, windows, reservation, routing and overrides are judgment.
ISO 30409:2016 is strategic workforce planning. It is not used for rostering, on-call or dispatch, per the Source Authority Pack section I.

ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 is cited only as a labelled ITSM structural analogue for demand (8.4.2), capacity (8.4.3), service level (8.3.3) and service request (8.6.2). It is not domain authority and is never cited for execution, scheduling or dispatch.

EN 17007 has no appointment, roster, what-if simulation, travel-routing or schedule-override process. RES.4, ACT.3, ACT.4, MAN.2, MAN.3, MAN.5, MAN.6, SER.4, DOC.6 and TOL.4 are the closest named processes. OPT is improvement of maintenance results, not plan simulation, and is not used for 3.1.3.

IEC 61968-6:2015 cl. 4.2 has no component for document management, procurement, health and safety, or fleet. Rosters sit on HR; tools and vehicles sit on MM; clearances sit on NO. The absence is recorded rather than inventing a code. SIM is Network operation simulation and is not used for work-demand scenarios.
IEC 61968-6 is electric-scoped. Gas distribution has no CIM work model; gas borrows the Work package here.

A clearance is produced by 18.4.4 against a switching plan approved at 18.2.2, under 29 CFR 1910.269(m). It is not a permit. 3.4.3 consumes the approved outage window from 18.2.2/18.2.3 as a schedule constraint; execution consumes the issued clearance. GFMAM 3.8 shutdown scheduling is 18.2, not 3.4.
3.1 forecasts WORK demand. APQC 10.2.2 Perform utility network planning (pcf_id 19213) is network demand and lives in 17.0. The two must not be collapsed.

APQC 14.4.2.2 Make appointment (pcf_id 19331) and 14.4.2.1 Schedule work (19330) sit under meter work. This model lifts both to the work lifecycle (3.3, 3.4). APQC 6.3.4.2 (pcf_id 10321) and 5.2.1 (20041) are cross-industry service analogues, not utility process authority.

Electric distribution has no federal prescriptive inspection interval (16 U.S.C. 824o). 3.4.3 names the state rule as the electric route. 'Business district' is undefined in Part 192 despite being the discriminator in 192.723.

No standard specifies appointment-window length, reservation behaviour, failure classes, crew size, district design, or a travel-time algorithm. SMRP 5.5.x resourcing-ratio names were not individually verified and are not used as measure names.

Overtime, standby and on-call PAY sit in 14.4.1. 3.2 consumes labour-agreement constraints and does not specify them. Live person status is 14.1.3; 3.5.4 is the scheduling view of that record plus equipment.
EN 15341 individual O&S indicator names and EN 17007 process-profile bodies remain paywalled and are cited clause-verified without paraphrase.

controls.text: 3.1 forecasts WORK demand and crew load. Network demand and capacity live in 17.0 / APQC 10.2.2 (pcf_id 19213). Do not treat a crew-capacity model as a network-capacity model.
ISO/IEC 20000-1 cl. 8.4.2 is an IT service analogue for demand management, not a field-work standard. Travel, credentials and geography are outside it.

merge_corrections.what: 32 citation statuses lowered to the ceiling in vocabulary.json source_status_ceiling.
merge_corrections.why: The submission marked paywalled standards 'verified'. It was following the Source Authority Pack, which asserted 'verified' for ISO 55001, ISO 9001 and IEC 61968-11 without this project holding those texts. Claude's own category 1.0 and 2.0 files had the same defect - 24 and 18 citations - and were corrected in the same commit. The ceiling is now enforced by validate_spec.py and clamped by the generators, so it cannot recur.
merge_corrections.not_a_content_change: No cite text, field or process was altered. Only the status claim attached to each citation.

merge_corrections.what: 27 EN 17007 citations raised from clause-verified to verified.
merge_corrections.why: EN 17007:2017 is the one standard this project holds in full - it is in Tim Evidence/ and clause 6 was read end to end on 2026-08-29, which is how the level-2 catalogue went from 11 processes to 101 and how two wrong clause numbers were found. A clause-and-code citation to it is verified, not clause-verified. The ceiling only ever lowers a status; raising one is deliberate, and this is it.
merge_corrections.not_a_content_change: No cite text, field or process was altered.

merge_corrections.what: citation form: a status may not claim more than the citation string supports. 'clause-verified' without a clause dropped to 'consensus'; an asserted absence dropped to 'judgment'.

ISO 55001:2024 cl. 8.3 was cited with ISO 9001's wording. The clause number is right; its title is Outsourcing. 'Control of externally provided processes, products and services' is ISO 9001:2015 cl. 8.4. A status of clause-verified asserts the clause number AND its title, so a borrowed title is an unearned status.
